- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.25) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by > 5% in first 10 days, model is likely underestimating volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for remaining days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1) triggers a 5–10% downward correction in forecast, especially if price is rising.
